title: Greenhouse Gas Auditing
desc: Measure, report and reduce greenhouse gas emissions for an organisation using recognised accounting scopes and data checks.
outcomes: Explain scopes 1, 2 and 3 and emission factors.
Collect activity data and calculate emissions.
Produce an inventory report and reduction plan.
task: Build a greenhouse gas inventory for one small organisation (practice case), with boundary, data, factors, hotspot analysis and reduction plan.
condition: A computer, a spreadsheet, public emission factors, two peers and a mentor. A practice dataset may be used.
standard: Boundary is stated; each number has unit and source; calculations reproduce; data quality is rated; plan has measurable targets; peers rate Meets or better.
who: Sustainability officers, finance staff, engineers, consultants in training.
evidence: boundary note, data sheet, inventory, hotspot chart, plan
modules: You cannot cut what you do not count.
Greenhouse gases trap heat; CO2 is the main one.
CO2e converts other gases to CO2 equivalent.
Reporting supports cost savings and customers.
Methane has a larger warming effect than CO2 per tonne.
Scope 1 direct; scope 2 purchased energy; scope 3 other chain.
Company vehicles are scope 1; electricity is scope 2.
Bills, meters, fuel logs, travel records.
Units must match: litres, kWh, km.
1,200 L x 2.68 kg CO2 per litre = 3,216 kg.
Efficient lighting cuts 8% for a payback of 2 years.
quiz: Direct, purchased energy, other chain emissions.
Purchased goods, travel, commuting or waste.
rubric: Every claim linked to a dated record and checked by a peer
Checked, dated and explained to others
next: wind and solar basics, water management, biofuels.
local: Reporting rules and emission factors differ by place and year.
ladder: L1: learner can say what CO2e means.
L6: learner can lead an inventory.
